rv.q: As difficult as it is to get mad at him for being so entertaining, you may nevertheless lament the deeper, more cohesive, and more incisive show this could have been.
Bryan Safi turns a lifetime of overthinking into a tight, anxious, audience-implicating hour that's less therapy session than victory lap.

cn.t: Safi's neurotic one-person show charms with self-deprecating humor and audience engagement, though its ADHD-fueled digressions prove distracting. Critics find the Emmy winner's anxious shtick delightful if unfocused.
